judge_assessment.explanation: Every judge claim checks out against the artifacts. The worksheet PDF does carry exactly 8 \problem blocks despite the tabular extraction noise, and I recomputed all of them independently: 34/35/36/__/38 -> 37; 56 count on 4 -> 60; two full ten-frames (20) plus 5 -> 25; 68+3 -> 71; 47+6 -> 53; 30/40/50/__ -> 60; just before 82 -> 81; Ana 45+4=49 versus Ben 47+3=50 -> '<'. Each agrees with verify.json and with the boxed value in answer_key.tex, and the study guide's six checks (44, 61, 40, 55, '>', '<') are right too. The 'slightly dense for K-1' artifact finding is fair: three skills plus a watch-out are packed onto one page. What the judge did not open is the Quick Answers bank on page 1 of the answer key, which reads '8. -' where it should read '<'. render_quick_answers._fmt() sympifies a string 'expected', sympy.sympify('<') raises SympifyError, and the entry drops into the '---' fallback reserved for manual items. The mathematics is correct; the grader's at-a-glance column loses the one comparison item on the sheet, which is also the sheet's hardest problem.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8 is the right synthesis item for this band and it is verified the right way: verify.json id 8 is compare(['45 + 4', '47 + 3'], order 'relation'), so the two counts the student must finish AND the symbol they choose are bound by one check, rather than the symbol alone being checked against hand-typed operands.

Problem 3 does what the 'concept-models' mode asks: the stem names the two full ten-frames as 20, and the key writes '10 + 10 = 20 dots. Counting forward 5 more gives 21, 22, 23, 24, 25' — the model is converted to notation and then counted on, instead of collapsing to 20 + 5.

Study guide Skill 3 ('Finish both counts first, then compare') is the direct teaching companion to worksheet problem 8, and its worked pair (30+5 vs 32+2) and try-it pair (60+3 vs 61+3) are both different from the worksheet's, so the guide teaches the method without giving the answer away.

root_causes.description: scripts/render_quick_answers.py resolves a string 'expected' by sympify+latex and falls back to a TeX em-dash when sympify raises. A bare relation symbol is not a sympifiable expression, so every compare problem whose order is 'relation' is silently banked as '---' — the marker the module documents as 'manual-only / see solution'. The verified answer exists and is correct; the grader's quick-reference column simply refuses to print it.
evidence: answer_key.pdf page 1, Quick Answers: '1. 37  2. 60  3. 25  4. 71  5. 53  6. 60  7. 81  8. -' — problem 8 is the only compare item and the only em-dash.
verify.json id 8: {"type": "compare", "order": "relation", "expected": "<"} — the value exists, and gate_log.txt step 5 records 'compare(45 + 4 vs 47 + 3) -> < (expected <)' as PASS.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt(): the str branch returns '---' on SympifyError, and sympy.sympify('<') raises SympifyError.

improvements.title: Quick Answers bank prints an em-dash instead of the verified relation symbol
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, handle relation strings in _fmt() BEFORE the sympify attempt: map '<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!=' (and the unicode forms) to '$<$', '$>$', '$=$', '$\le$', '$\ge$', '$\ne$'. sympy.sympify('<') raises SympifyError, so today every compare entry with "order": "relation" drops into the '---' fallback that exists for genuinely unrenderable values. Keep '---' for manual-only ids and for real sympify failures, so the fallback still means 'see the worked solution'.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py that renders a verify JSON of [{'id':1,'type':'compare','values':['3','7'],'order':'relation','expected':'<'}, {'id':2,'type':'compare','values':['9','4'],'order':'relation','expected':'>'}, {'id':3,'type':'manual','desc':'open'}] and asserts the bank lines are '$<$', '$>$' and '---' respectively. Today entries 1 and 2 both render '---', so the assertion fails; after the relation mapping it passes, and the manual id still prints '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: The answer key's grading column becomes complete for every compare item. On this sheet it restores 1 of 8 entries; across the shard the same fix also repairs 6 of 10 entries on curr-012, 2 of 6 on curr-034, 2 of 10 on curr-045 and 2 of 8 on curr-051, all of which currently ship a bank that omits the comparison answers.
improvements.risk: Low. Bank entries stay plain text (no \ans/\boxed), so check_answer_key.py's strict per-problem boxed-answer binding is untouched, and column_count() only sees a 3-char string. The only judgement call is math-mode wrapping of '='; both '=' and '$=$' set correctly inside the multicols block.

case_summary: A correct, well-modelled 8-problem counting-forward sheet for K-1. All eight worksheet answers, all six study-guide checks, the answer key's boxed values and the difficulty ramp (1,1,2,2,2,3,3,4) hold up under independent recomputation, and the count-then-compare closer (problem 8) is verified as a single compare over both counted expressions rather than as a bare symbol. The one defect is in the answer key's generated Quick Answers bank, which prints '-' for problem 8 because the renderer cannot sympify a relation symbol. That is a systemic renderer bug, not a content error, and the ACCEPT verdict stands.
